paper_title: How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media
caption: The average likes of headlines from different season groups
model_annotation: The chart illustrates the average number of likes (“Avg. Like #”) for headlines across five season-group bins labeled as the “Most similar group of posts.” The horizontal axis contains the categorical season-group intervals ordered left to right as (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450], with labels shown in parentheses and rotated diagonally; there is no legend. The vertical axis is the value axis labeled “Avg. Like #,” shown on a linear scale with visible tick labels at 400, 450, 500, 550, and 600 (regular 50-unit intervals), and the plotted range extends slightly above 600 to accommodate error bars. Each category is represented by a single light-blue bar with a thin dark outline and a vertical error bar: (0,90] is approximately 600 likes with an error bar extending to roughly the high-580s up to about 615–620; (90,180] is about 565–570 with an error bar spanning roughly the upper-540s to the mid-580s; (180,270] is about 570–575 with an error bar reaching from about the mid-540s to just under 600; (270,360] is about 595 with an error bar from roughly the upper-560s to around 625; and (360,450] is about 590 with an error bar from roughly the upper-550s to around 625. The bars are not visually emphasized beyond the uniform coloring and the inclusion of error bars, and they appear presented in increasing interval order rather than sorted by bar height.
